title: phasebound-primer: adaptive hotset reservoir and per-epoch kernel sampler
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a phase-aware primer that builds an adaptive hotset reservoir and a per-epoch kernel sampler. Improves p95 on mixed-seq workloads and provides a compact delta export for downstream attribution pipelines.
description:
Context and motivation: Production latency variability on heterogeneous sequence mixes shows recurring short-lived hotsets (small subset of prompt templates that dominate tail latency for minutes). Existing phase-agnostic samplers under-sample these short-lived regimes, so our regressions miss real-world tail behavior. This PR adds a lightweight 'phasebound primer' that detects epochal hotset shifts and maintains an adaptive hotset reservoir used to bias sampling for profiling and offline attributions. It also introduces a per-epoch kernel sampler that captures kernel-level hotpath attributions with prior-weighted sampling to stabilize estimates when hotsets are small.

What this PR does (summary): - Add adaptive hotset reservoir that tracks token/sequence signatures with time-decayed counts and an eviction policy tuned to short epochs. - Add per-epoch kernel sampler that ties sampled requests to kernel execution traces and aggregates per-kernel latency deltas across epochs. - Introduce a compact delta-exporter (ndjson) that emits per-epoch hotset summaries and kernel attribution records for downstream reporting pipelines (compatible with the existing telemetry ingestion). - Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for reservoir logic, integration harness that runs mixed-seq synthetic workload for 4 hours and produces p50/p95/p99 deltas vs baseline. - Observability: new metrics (hotset_size, reservoir_evictions, kernel_sample_rate, epoch_variance) and a dashboard json under docs/dashboards/phasebound-hotset.json.

Key results (from local benchmark lab runs): - Mixed-sequence synthetic workload (bimodal lengths 64/2048, 60/40 split) - Phasebound sampler increases hotset-capture recall from 0.42 to 0.86 for short-lived bursts (<= 5 minutes) - End-to-end p95 latency reduction in profiling runs: median 12% reduction vs prior sampler (profiling budget matched) - Estimated token-cost impact for profiling: 8% lower sampling cost to reach same attribution confidence compared to uniform sampling.

Commits (high-level): - 0a3b9f1: initial phasebound primer skeleton and interface - 5e7d2b4: reservoir core: time-decay counters, LRU eviction with reservoir caps - f2c1e88: per-epoch kernel sampler and trace attachment - a9d4c6f: delta-exporter ndjson schema + ingestion compatibility layer - 7f1b2a0: unit and integration tests + synthetic workload runner - c12b3d7: docs: dashboard + howto for running the new harness - 3d9f7e4: CI: flaky test stabilization and retry logic for histogram assertions

Files changed (high level): - src/samplers/phasebound_primer.py - src/samplers/reservoir.py - src/samplers/kernel_sampler.py - tools/bench/harness/phasebound_harness.py - tools/bench/reports/delta_exporter.py - test/samplers/test_reservoir.py - test/integration/test_phasebound_end2end.py - docs/dashboards/phasebound-hotset.json - .github/workflows/bench-ci.yml

Design notes and heuristics: - Reservoir uses a two-tiered structure: a small high-fidelity tier for very frequent signatures and an exploration tier for new arrivals; time-decay tunable ensures short hot bursts are retained long enough for a full epoch. - Kernel sampler applies a Bayesian prior (small pseudocount) per-kernel to avoid overfitting on single-sample spikes; priors are configurable per-deployment class. - Exporter emits compact ndjson records: epoch_id, hotset_hash, top_k_signatures, kernel_attributions (kernel_name, delta_ms, sample_weight). The schema is intentionally flat to integrate with the pipeline's mapreduce-style aggregators.

Review conversation (highlights): - Diego Rivera (review): "Nice modularization. Reservoir eviction needs a configurable upper bound per-tenant; can we avoid a global default that might OOM in extreme multi-tenant runs?" - Author (Maya): "Added per-tenant cap with a default safe-guard and documented the knob. See reservoir.py:TenantReservoirConfig." - Anika Bose (review): "Can you add integration smoke to the bench CI so we don't regress the exporter format? Also a note on ndjson schema versioning." - Author: "Added a smoke job in bench-ci and bump exporter to schema v1 with forward-compatible fields." - Liam O'Connor (approval): "R+ with minor nits; left one comment about metric naming." - Final author reply: "Addressed metric rename and added unit test for metric exposition."

CI and flaky behavior: - bench-ci pipeline: 3 runs during review. First run failed due to an unrelated histogram assertion (test_hist_aggregator) that times out under constrained runners; added retry+backoff and test isolation. Second run passed locally; third run on CI passed all jobs. Overall CI status: pass.

Rollout and migration notes: - Feature gated behind runtime flag sampler.phasebound.enabled (off by default for Dedicated until validated). - Backwards compatible: when disabled, sampler falls back to previous uniform/phase-agnostic sampler. - Telemetry consumers should be prepared for exporter schema v1; ingestion pipeline will ignore unknown fields.

Follow-ups and open items: - ENG-8891: instrument per-tenant memory accounting under high-multitenancy (tracked separately). - Measure end-to-end production impact under trace-sampled live traffic (we expect similar improvements but need to validate on live burst shapes). - Consider a lightweight on-device variant for constrained profiler agents.

Merge outcome: Squash merge to main; final merge commit: squash-33177-phasebound (author: Maya Chen). Changelog entry added.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration harness - [x] Benchmarks and summary - [x] Docs + dashboard - [x] CI green
